title: The business epic places the story in wave 1 while the service sits in wave 2
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-S8-E1021-APP: business_epic EP01, wave 1); _work/msr/context/S8.md (Service: wave 2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.6 W-MAP, R7.1)
section: Metadata Wave; s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s18 Traceability
description: The slice carries business epic EP01, whose W-MAP wave is 1, while rwb-deviation is a wave 2 service in the Arch v5 service table. Rule R5.6 says a story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service wave keeps the W-MAP wave and one conflict gap is raised per service and business epic. The metadata row keeps wave 1 as the plan gives it and the release date stays 30 November 2026 (tentative); no date is raised as a gap.
evidence: The split plan row for RWB-S8-E1021-APP gives business_epic EP01 and wave 1; context pack S8 gives the service wave as 2; Template and Rules v1 R5.6 maps EP01 to wave 1 and requires one conflict gap per service and business epic; R4 places S8 in wave 2.
owner_role: Programme planner with the S8 service owner
proposed: The programme keeps the W-MAP wave 1 for the business epic and plans the build against the wave 2 platform readiness of the service; if the service cannot be released in wave 1 the slice moves to wave 2 with its release date unchanged and no story content changes.

title: The plan gives this slice no build dependency while the DP table adds eight platform contract rows and two further contract rows
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-S8-E1021-APP: H empty, C RWB-P3-E1021-CON); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP table, R5.4, R5.7); _work/msr/context/S8.md (DP table, short form)
section: Metadata Depends on (build) and Contract dependencies; s3 Preconditions; s13 Pattern application
description: The DP table applied for DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP14, DP15 and DP19 adds eight platform H rows (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and two C rows (RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON), while the plan lists none of them and one C row only. The metadata rows are copied exactly from the plan as the work package requires, so the story keeps an empty build list and C = RWB-P3-E1021-CON, states the added rows in pattern application, and starts on Day 1 against their published baselines, which is what R5.7 rule 2 allows for a CON dependency and what the plan's Day-1 marker requires.
evidence: The split plan row for RWB-S8-E1021-APP gives H as an empty list and C as RWB-P3-E1021-CON only; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 lists the dependency each DP adds, including H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for DP-03, H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON for DP-04, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON for DP-07, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for DP-09, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON for DP-10, H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON for DP-14, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for DP-15 and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON for DP-19.
owner_role: Platform owner for the TPL, LIB, WF, DB, EVT and EDGE epics with the S8 service owner
proposed: The platform owner confirms which of the eight platform contract stories are published before the release date; the story builds against the published baselines and fakes and the metadata rows are corrected by the assembler if the plan is reissued.

title: No source publishes the operation names of the six rows this slice consumes
source: _work/msr/context/S8.md (ownership rows of S8: two REST operations, no consumed operation); Recovery Workbench TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2, T5.1, T5.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2.md (s12 Contract); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 4, 7 and 8; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9 Call-type summary
description: The slice consumes six rows and no source publishes the operation name of any of them: the rwb-case transfer request that performs the move, the rwb-case queue and capacity read, the reference-data read of LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, the rwb-decision package read, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-source-data case-facts read. The legacy story publishes only user-facing operations of the monolith, and the two operations the Ownership Map gives S8 are the deviation raise and the deviation outcome, so no service-to-service transfer operation exists in any source. The story therefore builds each row against a documented use, a placeholder name and a fake, and invents no path, parameter or transport.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S8 two REST operations and name no consumed operation; TSD S8 T-A.1 lists API-S8-001 and API-S8-002 only; TSD S8 T5.2 names the modules P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation; the legacy story publishes the manual transfer endpoint, the legal-hold endpoint, the TransferService interface and RuleEvaluator, all of them inside the monolith.
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data owner, P3 rwb-case owner, P4 rwb-access owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and the S8 service owner
proposed: Each owner publishes its operation name before the release date; until then the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use, and a published name replaces the placeholder in a minor contract version with no behaviour change.

title: No source says which service hosts the TRANSFER package evaluation after the split
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2.md (s2, s12, s13); Recovery Workbench Decision Log v10 (D-RCV-36 T1, T3, T5); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-S8-E1021-APP, secondary true); _work/msr/context/S8.md (ownership rows: no rule table, one workflow, DP-04)
section: s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s8 Business rules; s12.2; s13 Pattern application
description: The legacy story puts RuleEvaluator and package TRANSFER in P3, called by TransferService in the monolith. The plan assigns a slice of this legacy key to rwb-deviation as a secondary slice and lists DP-04, and the Ownership Map gives S8 no rule table, no rule package and only the deviation workflow, while the default ruling and the Ownership Map put the package registry in P7 rwb-decision. The story therefore hosts the evaluation of the deviation triggers in the embedded Drools kit of this service, reads the package and its version from rwb-decision, and requests the move from rwb-case; it does not restate the criteria of the legacy key that the primary slice owns.
evidence: Legacy s2 and s12 name RuleEvaluator and package TRANSFER as P3 components; D-RCV-36 T1 and T3 name one evaluator and no trigger list in code; the split plan marks RWB-S8-E1021-APP secondary; the context pack gives S8 no rule table, one workflow and the DP-04 row; Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings put the rule package registry with P7 rwb-decision.
owner_role: Solution architect with the S8 service owner and the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: The architect confirms the split of the evaluation between the two slices: the deviation triggers are evaluated in S8 against the package in force from P7, and the manual and the case-trigger paths stay with the primary slice in P3; the package stays one artefact with one version either way.

title: The TRANSFER rows that fire on the deviation triggers and the text of R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 are not published
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 (A2.4.3.1: R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02, R-DEV-03); Recovery Workbench TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 (T4: R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (DEV route set, 22 rules); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2.md (s3: package TRANSFER version TRF-2026.11 with at least 50 scenarios)
section: s3 Preconditions; s8 Business rules; s9 State transitions; s13 Build steps; s19 Out of scope
description: The engine evaluates package TRANSFER, whose rows are data of rwb-decision, and no source lists the rows that fires on DeviationRaised or DeviationCleared: the legacy story names TRF-001 to TRF-009 for its own trigger set and gives the package version TRF-2026.11 with at least 50 scenarios, and the FSD states only R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 of the owner assignment. The story reads the trigger rows and the row order from the package in force and never writes a row in code; the tests use the rule IDs the legacy story publishes as synthetic package data. The text of R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 is stated as a placeholder where the rule table needs it.
evidence: Legacy s3 gives package TRANSFER version TRF-2026.11 with at least 50 passing scenarios and each row holding trigger event, condition, target queue code and row order, and s7 lists TRF-001 to TRF-009 for eight named triggers; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 states R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 only; TSD S8 T4 lists R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 as OWNER_ASSIGNED rows of the DEVIATION machine without their text.
area: Rules and reference data, S8 rwb-deviation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S8
proposed: The rule owner publishes the DEV transfer rows and the text of R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 with the package version; the story then reads them unchanged and no code changes.

title: The event names of the P3 and P1 subscriptions are not published
source: _work/msr/context/S8.md (connection matrix row S8: E to P3 and R E to P1; ownership events EV-06 and EV-07 only); Recovery Workbench TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 (T5.3: DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2.md (s12: consumes EV-05, EV-06, EV-07, EV-09, EV-12, EV-16, EV-18)
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 3; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The connection matrix gives S8 an event subscription to P3 and to P1 and the legacy story names the seven trigger events by id only (EV-05, EV-06, EV-07, EV-09, EV-12, EV-16, EV-18). No source gives the Kafka event name of any case trigger on the per-service topics of the target architecture, and TSD S8 T5.3 publishes only the two events of S8 itself. The story declares both consumer groups against the placeholder, builds the TransferTrigger from the documented event codes, and fakes the subscription on Day 1.
evidence: The context pack connection matrix row S8 shows E in the P3 column and R E in the P1 column; TSD S8 T5.3 lists DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared as published and no consumed event; the legacy story names EV-05 to EV-18 with no event name and no topic.
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner, P1 rwb-source-data owner and the S8 service owner
proposed: The owners publish their event names on rwb.case.events.v1 and rwb.source-data.events.v1 before the release date; the consumer groups and the fact mapping are then bound to the published names with no change to the trigger logic.

title: No source fixes where this slice records the rule ID and the package version of a transfer
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2.md (s11: DF-CAS-021 recovery_case.rule_version, DF-WRK-040 assignment.transfer_reason_code); Recovery Workbench TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 (T3.1); _work/msr/context/S8.md (ownership: one table, deviation)
section: s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s8 BR5; s13 Deliverables
description: The legacy story writes the package version label to recovery_case.rule_version (DF-CAS-021) and the transfer reason to assignment.transfer_reason_code (DF-WRK-040), and both tables are rwb-case's after the split. TSD S8 T3.1 gives deviation ten columns of which none holds a rule ID, a package version or a transfer reference, and the Ownership Map gives S8 that one table. The story therefore records the rule ID, the package version and the from and to queue and owner in the decision record of DP-03, writes no column outside TSD S8 T3.1, and leaves the case-side label to rwb-case on the transfer request.
evidence: Legacy s11 lists DF-CAS-021 recovery_case.rule_version and DF-WRK-040 assignment.transfer_reason_code as writes; TSD S8 T3.1 lists DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 with no rule or transfer column; the context pack ownership rows give S8 the table deviation and no other.
owner_role: S8 service owner with the data steward of module S8 and the P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: If an audit read of the transfer rule per deviation row is required, the DB story adds a rule_id and a rule_version column to deviation; until then the decision record is the record of the transfer and the case label is P3's.
